## General

## 1 This practice direction applies to Technology and Construction Court claims (‘TCC claims’).

## TCC claims

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] 2.1 The following are examples of the types of claim which it may be appropriate to bring as TCC claims –

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (a) building or other construction disputes, including claims for the enforcement of the decisions of adjudicators under the Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (b) engineering disputes;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (c) claims by and against engineers, architects, surveyors, accountants and other specialised advisers relating to the services they provide;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (d) claims by and against local authorities relating to their statutory duties concerning the development of land or the construction of buildings;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (e) claims relating to the design, supply and installation of computers, computer software and related network systems;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (f) claims relating to the quality of goods sold or hired, and work done, materials supplied or services rendered;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (g) claims between landlord and tenant for breach of a repairing covenant;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (ga) claims between landlords and contract-holders for breach of obligation to repair dwellings under the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (h) claims between neighbours, owners and occupiers of land in trespass, nuisance etc;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (i) claims relating to the environment (for example, pollution cases);

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (j) claims arising out of fires;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (k) claims involving taking of accounts where these are complicated; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] (l) challenges to decisions of arbitrators in construction and engineering disputes including applications for permission to appeal and appeals.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > TCC claims] 2.2 A claim given as an example in paragraph 2.1 will not be suitable for this specialist list unless it demonstrates the characteristics in rule 60.1(3). Similarly, the examples are not exhaustive and other types of claim may be appropriate to this specialist list.

## How to start a TCC claim

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > How to start a TCC claim] 3.1 TCC claims must be issued in the High Court or in a County Court hearing centre specified in this practice direction.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > How to start a TCC claim] 3.2 The claim form must be marked in the top right hand corner ‘Technology and Construction Court (KBD)’ below the words ‘In the High Court of Justice, Business and Property Courts [in/of   ]’. In the County Court the claim form must be marked “Business and Property Courts work”.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > How to start a TCC claim] 3.3 TCC claims brought in the High Court outside London may be issued in any district registry, but it is preferable that wherever possible they should be issued in one of the following district registries, in which a TCC judge will usually be available –

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > How to start a TCC claim] Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, Chester, Exeter, Leeds, Liverpool, Manchester, Mold, Newcastle upon Tyne and Nottingham.

## 3.4 The County Court hearing centres in which a TCC claim may be issued are the following –

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > 3.4 The County Court hearing centres in which a TCC claim may be issued are the following –] Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, Central London, Chester, Exeter, Leeds, Liverpool, Manchester, Mold, Newcastle upon Tyne and Nottingham.

## Applications before proceedings are issued

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Applications before proceedings are issued] 4.1 A party who intends to issue a TCC claim must make any application before the claim form is issued to a TCC judge.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Applications before proceedings are issued] 4.2 The written evidence in support of such an application must state that the proposed claim is a TCC claim.

## Transfer of proceedings

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Transfer of proceedings] 5.1 Where no TCC judge is available to deal with a claim which has been issued in a High Court District Registry or one of the County Court hearing centres listed in paragraph 3.4 above, the claim may be transferred –

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Transfer of proceedings] (1) if it has been issued in a District Registry, to another District Registry or to the High Court in London; or

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Transfer of proceedings] (2) if it has been issued in the County Court, to another County Court hearing centre where a TCC judge would be available.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Transfer of proceedings] 5.2 Paragraph 5.1 is without prejudice to the court’s general powers to transfer proceedings under Part 30.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Transfer of proceedings] (Rule 30.5(3) provides that an application for the transfer of proceedings to or from a specialist list must be made to a judge dealing with claims in that list.)

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Transfer of proceedings] 5.3 A party applying to a TCC judge to transfer a claim to the TCC specialist list must give notice of the application to the court in which the claim is proceeding, and a TCC judge will not make an order for transfer until he is satisfied that such notice has been given.

## Assignment of claim to a TCC judge

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Assignment of claim to a TCC judge] 6.1 When a TCC claim is issued or an order is made transferring a claim to the TCC specialist list, the court will assign the claim to a named TCC judge (‘the assigned TCC judge’) who will have the primary responsibility for the case management of that claim.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Assignment of claim to a TCC judge] 6.2 All documents relating to the claim must be marked in similar manner to the claim form with the words ‘Technology and Construction Court’ and the name of the assigned TCC judge.

## Applications

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Applications] 7.1 An application should normally be made to the assigned TCC judge. If the assigned TCC judge is not available, or the court gives permission, the application may be made to another TCC judge.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Applications] 7.2 If an application is urgent and there is no TCC judge available to deal with it, the application may be made to any judge who, if the claim were not a TCC claim, would be authorised to deal with the application.

## Case management conference

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] 8.1 The court will fix a case management conference within 14 days of the earliest of these events –

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (1) the filing of an acknowledgment of service;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (2) the filing of a defence; or

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (3) the date of an order transferring the claim to a TCC.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] 8.2 When the court notifies the parties of the date and time of the case management conference, it will at the same time send each party a case management information sheet and a case management directions form.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (The case management information sheet and the case management directions form are in the form set out in Appendixes A and B to this practice direction.)

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] 8.3 Not less than two days before the case management conference, each party must file and serve on all other parties –

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (1) completed copies of the case management information sheet and case management directions form; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (2) an application notice for any order which that party intends to seek at the case management conference, other than directions referred to in the case management directions form.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] 8.4 The parties are encouraged to agree directions to propose to the court by reference to the case management directions form.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] 8.5 If any party fails to file or serve the case management information sheet and the case management directions form by the date specified, the court may –

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (1) impose such sanction as it sees fit; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (2) either proceed with or adjourn the case management conference.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] 8.6 The directions given at the case management conference will normally include the fixing of dates for –

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (1) any further case management conferences;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (2) a pre-trial review;

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (3) the trial of any preliminary issues that it orders to be tried; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Case management conference] (4) the trial.

## Pre-trial review

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Pre-trial review] 9.1 When the court fixes the date for a pre-trial review it will send each party a pre-trial review questionnaire.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Pre-trial review] (The pre-trial review questionnaire is in the form set out in Appendix C to this practice direction).

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Pre-trial review] 9.2 Each party must file and serve on all other parties completed copies of the questionnaire not less than two days before the date fixed for the pre-trial review.

## 9.3 The parties are encouraged to agree directions to propose to the court.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > 9.3 The parties are encouraged to agree directions to propose to the court.] 9.4 If any party fails to return or exchange the questionnaire by the date specified the court may –

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > 9.3 The parties are encouraged to agree directions to propose to the court.] (1) impose such sanction as it sees fit; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > 9.3 The parties are encouraged to agree directions to propose to the court.] (2) either proceed with or adjourn the pre-trial review.

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > 9.3 The parties are encouraged to agree directions to propose to the court.] 9.5 At the pre-trial review, the court will give such directions for the conduct of the trial as it sees fit.

## Listing

[This practice direction supplements Part 60 > Listing] 10 The provisions about listing questionnaires and listing in Part 29 and Practice Direction 29 do not apply to TCC claims.

## Trial

## 11.1 Whenever possible the trial of a claim will be heard by the assigned TCC judge.

## 11.2 A TCC claim may be tried at any place where there is a TCC judge available to try the claim.
